business_items.title: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now
business_items.summary: Techies are building technology that can advance all aspects of the world — but can they protect their hearts? That's the vulnerability that honey pots exploit.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
Techies are building technology that can advance all aspects of the world — but can they protect their hearts? That's the vulnerability that honey pots exploit.

Even as the fall-out for Nvidia over Jensen Huang’s alleged honey-trap scandal is still unfolding, Silicon Valley has yet to reckon with a new reality: many more people among them are at risk.

“Nobody briefs founders on counterintelligence,” Aaron Brown, a former senior CIA officer and current founder of the software company Lumbra, told TechCrunch.

That’s because historically honey traps have been associated with politicians, the military, and national intelligence — the people “behind clearances and a workforce trained to expect an approach,” from spies and other attackers.

But now many of the most valuable secrets “sit inside companies building chips, models, and infrastructure,” Brown says, adding that a spy “wants what the CEO can touch. The roadmap, the export decisions, the customer list, who gets the technology. The CEO is the shortest path to all of it.”

Huang has been accused of falling for just such a honey trap by having an affair with Alice Huang. She’s a former executive of a Singapore neocloud who’s been accused of being a Chinese spy and of smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of restricted Nvidia chips into China.

After the Huang allegations broke, jokes flooded the internet about which tech CEO will be next, but it’s not just CEOs and founders who are at risk. The WSJ reported that OpenAI started warning its employees about outsiders trying to cozy up to them in search of company secrets. Anyone with access to sensitive information — from board members to executive assistants — can be the target of a honey trap.

And typically, the attackers aren’t lovers. Friendship is actually the oldest honey-trap scheme around, Brown said.

Honey traps gain access to their targets as investors, customers, recruiters, and consultancies. Their requests look legitimate on paper and don’t need their targets to fall in love. “They need you to feel comfortable talking,” Brown said. “They last longer because nobody’s looking.”

What’s interesting, too, is the irony. So many tech founders are moving to automate and digitize so much of human life and yet remain vulnerable to the oldest bug around, a person who preys on the human need to be understood by others.

“Why fight through a firewall when you can get close to the person who can open doors, influence decisions, or make requests nobody wants to question?” Perry Carpenter, a criminologist and chief deception strategist at KnowBe4, told TechCrunch.

Once targets realize they have been compromised, the threat can escalate: attackers now have a means of blackmail.

Another irony: AI has made honey-trapping much easier and cheaper. Planning a scheme used to take months or years of research, crafting a persona, knowing the target, and executing a plan. These days, it’s easy to use AI to research a target, generate fake social profiles, fake backgrounds, even fake voice calls.

“AI can help sustain an entire fictional backstory,” Carpenter said. “The technology helps set the stage, but the deception ultimately plays out through human relationships.”

The AI industry “became a national security industry faster than its culture caught up,” Brown said.

“Part of being honey-trapped is not knowing,” he added. “It doesn’t feel like manipulation. It feels genuine, even lucky.”

Carpenter said a good first step is looking for unusual patterns. Note, for instance, “coincidental encounters that happen a little too often,” he said. There are also obvious signs, like persistent curiosity about work and colleagues, or requesting secrecy about meeting up, and pressing for introductions or information.

Bigger red flags include if someone’s requests are getting bigger, pushing the boundaries of what you usually would be uncomfortable doing. “A simple gut check,” Brown said. “Would this person still be around if you lost your job tomorrow?”

It also helps to try and understand when emotions might be influencing a decision. Carpenter suggests putting up a clear boundary between one’s personal and professional life. Within companies, it also helps to “eliminate executive exceptionalism,” he said, the idea that the rules don’t apply to people in power at the company.

business_items.title: A transcription firm used by police, prosecutors, and tech giants exposed customer data online
business_items.summary: Exclusive: A simple security lapse exposed transcriptions of police interviews and bodycam footage on a cloud server without a password.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
Exclusive: A simple security lapse exposed transcriptions of police interviews and bodycam footage on a cloud server without a password.

A transcription company that caters to law enforcement, government departments, and Silicon Valley tech giants has resolved a security lapse after leaving a large amount of internal data, including customer transcriptions and their source materials, exposed to the web.

The data security lapse at San Francisco-based Tigerfish exposed transcriptions of police interviews, body-cam footage, and customers’ raw audio and video footage. The exposed data also included invoices of the company’s customers, which include police departments and prosecutors’ offices.

According to Anurag Sen , a good faith security researcher who found the data, the files were located on an Amazon-hosted (S3) cloud server that was openly listed and accessible to anyone via an easy-to-guess web address — no passwords needed.

The security lapse underscores how simple flaws or misconfigurations can result in sensitive information getting exposed online, especially as AI makes it easier to uncover weaknesses that can put companies and their data at risk.

Sen discovered the exposed data online in October and alerted the company to the issue, but did not hear back. Sen later provided details to TechCrunch in an effort to flag the incident with the company for resolution.

Sen, 30, is no stranger to TechCrunch. For the past decade, he has searched for sensitive datasets exposed online with the goal of notifying the companies and organizations that their information is open to the internet. Like many security researchers, much of his efforts are driven by a duty to secure the internet, and he describes his work as an “unpaid air-traffic controller.”

From his island home in Indonesia, Sen has uncovered sensitive U.S. military emails spilling from a compartmentalized Department of Defense cloud server; databases exposing reams of customer records ; the inner workings of a country’s national license plate surveillance system ; and public systems that inadvertently sent out streams of SMS codes used by people around the world to log into their online accounts.

Given Sen’s propensity for finding often highly confidential information online, we verified the source of the leak and the data, and contacted Tigerfish.

Soon after making contact, Tigerfish secured its exposed S3 cloud bucket.

“We’ve blocked all public access to the bucket you identified, including directory listings and individual files,” Tigerfish president, Adam Goldberg, said in an email. “We’ve also verified that all of our other S3 buckets are blocked to public access.”

“We’re continuing to review and strengthen our storage security more broadly,” added Goldberg.

The company said that Sen’s email disclosing the data leak was caught in its spam filter.

It’s unclear if the company has notified its customers. Tigerfish did not respond to a follow-up email.

Discoveries of exposed datasets have consumed a large part of Sen’s early cybersecurity career so far. He scours the web daily using automated scanners and specialist search engines to identify databases, cloud storage, or other sensitive information that likely shouldn’t be left unprotected online.

The modern web runs on absolute trust, he said, and operates under the notion that the world’s data is kept secure. But he described how his findings reveal the reality of how “fragile” the internet is behind the scenes.

Despite the recent focus on how AI is accelerating people’s ability to discover vulnerabilities, Sen said that many of the data leaks and exposures that he finds come down to basic human errors.

“An engineer spinning up a test cloud database on a Friday, disabling authentication to test an API, and forgetting to shut the door before heading into the weekend,” was just one example, he recounted.

Sen’s findings over the years highlight the ongoing problems caused by such security mistakes, just as the new wave of vibe-coding and AI-generated development is creating new security problems due to insecure and unchecked code deployed to the web.

business_items.title: The US national cyber director is stepping down
business_items.summary: The news comes as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages, the causes of which are still unknown.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
The news comes as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages, the causes of which are still unknown.

White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross will be stepping down from his role, Axios reported. The news comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages whose cause remains unknown.

Cairncross, the president’s principal adviser on national cybersecurity policy and strategy, took office in August 2025. Since then, he has met with top AI leaders and helped the Trump administration make key AI decisions, according to Axios. The outlet also reports that the split between Cairncross and the White House was amicable, and his departure was timed so that the White House could nab a Senate confirmation for his role before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Cairncross, a lawyer and longtime Republican operative, had no cybersecurity background when the Senate confirmed him 59–35. He previously served as the Republican National Committee’s chief operating officer and, during Trump’s first term, as CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a federal foreign aid agency. The office hasn’t been around long; Congress created it in early 2021, and Cairncross was only its third Senate-confirmed director. The first director, Chris Inglis, left after about 19 months, and the job then went about 10 months without a permanent director.

business_items.title: These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style
business_items.summary: Are the recent outages in the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms really a coincidence? There's actually likely something deeper going on, cybersecurity experts say.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
Are the recent outages in the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms really a coincidence? There's actually likely something deeper going on, cybersecurity experts say.

It’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms. In the past two weeks, the U.S.’s top businesses have faced technical outages that have disrupted the systems that run everyday life.

Apple Pay went down. NASA’s internal communication network went down. The FAA had to ground all flights for hours (only the third time in history since 9/11), and Microsoft was hit with an outage that took down Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for nearly two days.

The first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago. Here in the U.S., the director of National Intelligence said these outages don’t seem related to state-sponsored terrorism, while President Trump called the issues “individual events.” Many of the companies themselves have said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks or AI attacks, but tech issues.

Only, there’s the fact that they all struck within a short timespan of each other, and just a few weeks after Cybersecurity’s so-called “Black October,” when a slew of also-unrelated cybersecurity incidents occurred on October 21, striking PHP, Node.js, LiteLLM, more.

While there’s no reason to view these outages as cyberattacks, there may be more than coincidence going on: It’s giving AI-native Y2K, frankly.

Dave DeWalt, an investor who worked in cybersecurity for more than three decades (including as president and CEO of McAfee and as vice chairman of the CISA Advisory Council for the Department of Homeland Security), also thinks it’s probably AI-related.

The technical outages are most likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” and that “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before through AI tools like Mythos and others,” he told TechCrunch.

The thing is, many of these technical flaws have always existed, but because AI is surfacing them so fast, enterprises are rushing to fix them before bad actors can exploit them. “That surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he said.

This was, perhaps, the first moment when legacy meets modern, Anusha Iyer, a software engineer and founder of the security startup Corsha, told TechCrunch. “These industrial systems were never designed to be connected, let alone securely connected in the way we are pushing them to be today,” she said.

Virginia Senator Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intel Committee, came to a similar conclusion (although investigations are still underway as to what could be happening). “These disruptions should serve as a wake-up call. It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” the senator wrote on X .

AI is reshaping how software is built, deployed, and operated, on a scale where everyone feels the sharp learning curve. Iyer cited the FAA outage as an example of legacy tech that is not as sophisticated or advanced as the technologies companies are trying to merge it with.

In less technical terms, she said the outage may have been caused (and preliminary findings point to this) when the FAA was trying to modernize its telecommunications infrastructure and the transition overwhelmed parts of its legacy hardware, where the new tech likely operated at a normal modern capacity while the legacy hardware couldn’t keep up.

When looked at this way, she said, AI is actually getting the bad rep. “It’s not rapid adoption of AI yet causing these outages,” she said. “The fault is the rushed mix of the legacy and modern systems without a clear understanding of operational and cyber risk or the ability to gatekeep and protect the legacy systems.”

Organizations need a more steadfast approach to AI adoption, including more testing and prioritizing what needs to be fixed and when, DeWalt said.

Iyer added, “These industrial systems need to be segmented more tightly and more access controlled, so as modern systems are introduced, it can be phased in and risk mitigated.”

Actually, there might be a silver lining to all of this for companies (and for venture investors). DeWalt said he’d rather see these U.S. enterprises find and patch their flaws, even in this messy way, than have bad actors find and exploit those vulnerabilities in AI warfare that could cause even more national security issues.

And maybe some aspiring founders were inspired by them. DeWalt expects a rise in companies focused on “AI-driven vulnerability management, autonomous remediation, safe patch testing and deployment, and resilience for the systems that keep critical infrastructure running,” he said.

“There’s real pain in this transition as we’ve seen in the past week,” DeWalt said. “But there’s also enormous opportunity for the companies that help organizations move at AI speed without breaking things.”

business_items.title: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order
business_items.summary: The U.K. tribunal's ruling rejected London's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
The U.K. tribunal's ruling rejected London's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.

The U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.

The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.

The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.

The ruling comes a year after the U.K. government reportedly demanded that Apple build a backdoor to allow U.K. authorities access to customer data anywhere in the world. Details of the so-called “technical capabilities notice,” which are issued under strict non-disclosure rules, leaked to the media, which drew ire from White House officials and U.S. lawmakers who criticized the effort , arguing that the U.K. order would put Americans’ privacy at risk.

California-based Apple refused the order, and blocked U.K. users from switching on its Advanced Data Protection data-encryption feature for iCloud, rather than comply with the demand. The U.K.’s secret order was later narrowed to allow access to British nationals’ data stored in Apple’s encrypted cloud, and Apple also challenged this second order.

Prior to the ruling, Apple was legally barred from disclosing the order, even after details leaked. When reached for comment, Apple told TechCrunch that it welcomes the decision to make public the fact that the U.K. Home Office issued a technical capability notice.

Apple previously said that it has “never built a backdoor or master key” to any of its products or services and “never will.”

A spokesperson for the U.K. Home Office, which has yet to confirm the existence of a notice, did not respond to a request for comment.

Rights group Liberty International, which brought the legal challenge on behalf of two individuals, said that this is the first known time that the government has been compelled to confirm the existence of a secret technical order.

A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year.

business_items.title: Palmer Luckey doesn’t deny that he’s a prepper
business_items.summary: The Anduril founder said Wednesday that Americans should always have three days of food, water, and medicine — just in case.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
The Anduril founder said Wednesday that Americans should always have three days of food, water, and medicine — just in case.

Defense mogul Palmer Luckey — whose $90 billion drone and weapons startup Anduril is flush with government contracts — is still the kind of guy who prepares for the worst.

During Luckey’s conversation with Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the billionaire implied that Americans should batten down the hatches in case there are rough times ahead. Luckey himself has taken steps to prepare for a potential cataclysmic event, he said.

The conversation took place against the backdrop of a series of recent large-scale outages — at Apple , at Microsoft , at the NSA , and at the Federal Aviation Administration — that have led to concerns that America may be under attack by cyberthreat actors. The government has said that this is not the case , but Luckey cryptically teased that there may be more to the story.

“Look, all the 4chan schizo posters are like 12 hours ahead of the mainstream media on this. You guys are going to find out what’s going on soon enough,” he said.

Sorkin also asked Luckey to expound on comments made backstage “about what might be a cyber war that seems to be going on around us.”

Luckey described a “mismatch” between the sophisticated AI-powered cyberattacks that exist today and “old, outdated systems that are not able to adopt technology as quickly as it is developed.” He added: “I think people are going to have to pick up the pace. It’s time to start running.”

“What does that mean? Are you a prepper?” Sorkin asked.

Luckey didn’t deny the characterization. “I own a missile base 200 feet underground,” he answered, to audience laughter. “It’s a funny joke, but a missile base is actually a pretty bad way to run from the apocalypse. Everyone knows exactly where you are, and they [bases] are designed to take a hit from a nuclear weapon, a blast overpressure event.”

However, he had some qualifications on the prepper label. “The point is, like everyone should have three days of water. Everyone should have three days of dry food. If you have prescription medication, don’t go refill it when you run out. Make sure you refill it 72 hours before you run out.”

“People used to be taught this in middle school, and now everyone who remembers that is treated like a nut,” he added.

It should be pointed out that preparing for the apocalypse is not necessarily a new interest for Luckey. In 2017, a person familiar with the billionaire described him as a “prepper” and the bunker that was broached Wednesday is one of several decommissioned Cold War era underground bases that Luckey has purchased over the years. In 2024, he revealed that his massive video game collection is housed in one of them.

business_items.title: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’
business_items.summary: The Anduril co-founder says outdated technology is leaving systems vulnerable to a new wave of AI-enabled attacks.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
The Anduril co-founder says outdated technology is leaving systems vulnerable to a new wave of AI-enabled attacks.

AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, Palmer Luckey warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Addressing the recent spate of tech outages, the Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder argued that older systems are struggling to keep pace with the new hacking capabilities enabled by AI and warned it was time to quicken the pace of securing our defenses.

“We’re seeing the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools allowing for the creation of various exploits,” he said.

While government officials largely attributed the latest set of technical issues to companies rushing to patch their systems to protect against the new vulnerabilities AI has discovered, Luckey focused on the underlying security challenges facing organizations using outdated technology.

Luckey explained that U.S. adversaries are currently exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and our defense capabilities. These attacks are being carried out for both strategic and financial reasons, and North Korea was particularly involved, he added.

The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, noted that U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance had canceled his appearance at the Times’ conference this week because of the recent tech outages, saying he now had to attend meetings about the matter.

Given the situation, Sorkin asked Luckey how worried we should be about all this.

“It depends on how well prepared you are,” was Luckey’s answer. (He then ominously warned, “You guys are going to find out what’s going on soon enough.”)

The tech executive argued that AI could ultimately give defenders the upper hand, but they’d have to move more quickly.

“In the long run, the advantages are going to accrue to the side that is most effectively using AI for defense,” Luckey said. “With the people who say that everything can be hacked — they are right, for now. That actually may be the case with certain new techniques that are coming along. But as of right now, there’s a mismatch between the attackers who are very fast-moving and using technology and old, outdated systems that are not able to adopt technology as quickly as it is developed,” Luckey continued.

“And I think … people are going to have to pick up the pace,” he said. “It’s time to start running.”

business_items.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
business_items.summary: Citi is the latest major financial institution to put the breaks on personal finance AI agents.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
Citi is the latest major financial institution to put the breaks on personal finance AI agents.

Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.

AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.

But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.

“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”

JPMorgan and Bank of America , the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eighth largest bank, changed its terms today.

Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tool leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account. Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.

As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector. But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.

Anthropic’s approach is telling: The personal finance tool it launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”

Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat. Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins. But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway. Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.

The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything from car-hailing to food service , and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.

business_items.summary: Two British hackers face lengthy prison sentences for hacks that broke into the Grand Theft Auto gamemaker and for stealing millions in crypto.
business_items.confidence: Reported; verify material claims against company announcements and regulatory filings
business_items.details:
Two British hackers face lengthy prison sentences for hacks that broke into the Grand Theft Auto gamemaker and for stealing millions in crypto.

Two British hackers are facing lengthy prison sentences for separate hacks as part of their roles in long-running, prolific cybercriminal hacking groups. The two are accused of hacks that stole millions of dollars in cryptocurrency and leaked pre-release footage from Grand Theft Auto VI.

Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, Scotland, has been sentenced to six years by a U.S. court after he was extradited to the United States in 2025. Buchanan was accused of stealing at least $11 million in cryptocurrency from dozens of companies as part of a phishing scheme. The attacks would impersonate IT helpdesks and call up unsuspecting employees and trick them into giving over their credentials, which the hackers would use to break in and steal cryptocurrency.

Meanwhile, Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, England, has pleaded guilty to several cyberattacks that he carried out while a teenager. One hack included the theft of data and extortion of Rockstar Games, the maker of Grand Theft Auto VI, which was released Wednesday after several delays .

Kurtaj was previously ordered by a U.K. court to be detained indefinitely after deeming him unable to stand trial due to his autism diagnosis and his perceived high hacking risk to the public. But U.K. authorities, tasked with charging Kurtaj with cybercrime offenses, confirmed Monday that he had admitted to several hacks, including leaking footage of the long-awaited video game, and would subsequently face a public trial.

U.K. authorities confirmed earlier reporting that Kurtaj hacked several companies, including while he was confined to a hotel amid police protection from rival criminal gangs. The authorities said Kurtaj used an Amazon Fire TV stick to hack the companies, which breached his bail conditions.

Both Buchanan and Kurtaj were members of overlapping cybercriminal groups, dubbed 0ktapus, Lapsus$, and later Scattered Spider . These prolific hacking gangs mostly consist of teenagers and young male adults, lending to the term “advanced persistent teenagers,” whose focus and motivations were to steal as much money as possible through various cyberattacks.

Over the years, the hackers were collectively responsible for hundreds of cyberattacks targeting big companies, including Coinbase , DoorDash , Mailchimp , and Nvidia .

By late 2024, both U.K. and U.S. authorities say they had indicted five of the hackers whom they believed were key members of the hacking groups, including Buchanan. The U.S. Department of Justice said this week that Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in this case.

cisa_kev_catalog.product: Pulse Connect Secure and Pulse Policy Secure
cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Ivanti Pulse Connect Secure and Policy Secure Command Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Ivanti Pulse Connect Secure and Policy Secure allows an authenticated attacker from the admin web interface to inject and execute commands.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Qualcomm Multiple Chipsets Detection of Error Condition Without Action Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Multiple Qualcomm chipsets contain a detection of error condition without action vulnerability when improper handling of address deregistration on failure can lead to new GPU address allocation failure.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Qualcomm Multiple Chipsets Use-After-Free Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Multiple Qualcomm Chipsets contain a use after free vulnerability due to improper handling of memory mapping of multiple processes simultaneously.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: rConfig OS Command Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: rConfig lib/ajaxHandlers/ajaxAddTemplate.php contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute OS commands via shell metacharacters in the fileName POST parameter.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Realtek AP-Router SDK Buffer Overflow Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Realtek AP-Router SDK HTTP web server boa contains a buffer overflow vulnerability due to unsafe copies of some overly long parameters submitted in the form that lead to denial-of-service (DoS).
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Roundcube Webmail File Disclosure Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Roundcube Webmail contains a file disclosure vulnerability caused by insufficient input validation in conjunction with file-based attachment plugins, which are used by default.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SaltStack Salt Path Traversal Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SaltStack Salt contains a path traversal vulnerability in the salt-master process ClearFuncs which allows directory access to authenticated users. Salt users who follow fundamental internet security guidelines and best practices are not affected by this vulnerability.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SaltStack Salt Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SaltStack Salt contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the salt-master process ClearFuncs due to improperly validating method calls. The vulnerability allows a remote user to access some methods without authentication, which can be used to retrieve user tokens from the salt master and/or run commands on salt minions. Salt users who follow fundamental internet security guidelines and best practices are not affected by this vulnerability.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SaltStack Salt Shell Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SaltStack Salt allows an unauthenticated user with network access to the Salt API to use shell injections to run code on the Salt API using the SSH client. This vulnerability affects any users running the Salt API.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SAP Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Path Traversal Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SAP Customer Relationship Management (CRM) contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows an attacker to exploit insufficient validation of path information provided by users.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SAP NetWeaver Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms Invoker Servlet does not require authentication, allowing for remote code execution via a HTTP or HTTPS request.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SAP NetWeaver XML External Entity (XXE) Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms contains an unspecified vulnerability in BC-BMT-BPM-DSK which allows remote, authenticated users to conduct XML External Entity (XXE) attacks.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SAP NetWeaver Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability allowing unauthenticated access to execute configuration tasks and create administrative users.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SAP Solution Manager Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SAP Solution Manager User Experience Monitoring contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which results in complete compromise of all SMDAgents connected to the Solution Manager.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SAP NetWeaver Directory Traversal Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms contains a directory traversal vulnerability via a ..\ (dot dot backslash) in the fileName parameter to CrashFileDownloadServlet. This allows remote attackers to read files.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SIMalliance Toolbox Browser Command Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SIMalliance Toolbox Browser contains an command injection vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to retrieve location and IMEI information or execute a range of other attacks by modifying the attack message.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SolarWinds Orion Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SolarWinds Orion API contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute API commands.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SolarWinds Serv-U Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SolarWinds Serv-U contains an unspecified memory escape vulnerability which can allow for remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SolarWinds Virtualization Manager Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SolarWinds Virtualization Manager allows for privilege escalation through leveraging a misconfiguration of sudo.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Sonatype Nexus Repository Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Sonatype Nexus Repository contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SonicWall Email Security Improper Privilege Management Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SonicWall Email Security contains an improper privilege management vulnerability that allows an attacker to create an administrative account by sending a crafted HTTP request to the remote host. This vulnerability has known usage in a SonicWall Email Security exploit chain along with CVE-2021-20022 and CVE-2021-20023 to achieve privilege escalation.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SonicWall SMA100 SQL Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SonicWall SMA100 contains a SQL injection vulnerability allowing an unauthenticated user to gain read-only access to unauthorized resources.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SonicWall Email Security Unrestricted Upload of File Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SonicWall Email Security contains an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows a post-authenticated attacker to upload a file to the remote host. This vulnerability has known usage in a SonicWall Email Security exploit chain along with CVE-2021-20021 and CVE-2021-20023 to achieve privilege escalation.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SonicWall Email Security Path Traversal Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SonicWall Email Security contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows a post-authenticated attacker to read files on the remote host. This vulnerability has known usage in a SonicWall Email Security exploit chain along with CVE-2021-20021 and CVE-2021-20022 to achieve privilege escalation.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: SonicWall SSLVPN SMA100 SQL Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: SonicWall SSLVPN SMA100 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows remote exploitation for credential access by an unauthenticated attacker.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Sophos SFOS SQL Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Sophos Firewall operating system (SFOS) firmware contains a SQL injection vulnerability when configured with either the administration (HTTPS) service or the User Portal is exposed on the WAN zone. Successful exploitation may cause remote code execution to exfiltrate usernames and hashed passwords for the local device admin(s), portal admins, and user accounts used for remote access (but not external Active Directory or LDAP passwords).
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Sumavision EMR Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Sumavision Enhanced Multimedia Router (EMR) contains a cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability allowing the creation of users with elevated privileges as administrator on a device.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Symantec Messaging Gateway Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Symantec Messaging Gateway contains an unspecified vulnerability which can allow for remote code execution. With the ability to perform remote code execution, an attacker may also desire to perform privilege escalating actions.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: TeamViewer Desktop Bypass Remote Login Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: TeamViewer Desktop allows for bypass of remote-login access control because the same AES key is used for different customers' installations. If an attacker were to know this key, they could decrypt protected information stored in registry or configuration files or decryption of the Unattended Access password to the system (which allows for remote login to the system).
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX and Sitefinity Cryptographic Weakness Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX and Sitefinity have a cryptographic weakness in Telerik.Web.UI.dll that can be exploited to disclose encryption keys (Telerik.Web.UI.DialogParametersEncryptionKey and/or the MachineKey), perform cross-site-scripting (XSS) attacks, compromise the ASP.NET ViewState, and/or upload and download files.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Tenda AC11 Router Stack Buffer Overflow Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Tenda AC11 devices contain a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in /goform/setmac which allows attackers to execute code via a crafted post request.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Tenda AC1900 Router AC15 Model Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Tenda AC1900 Router AC15 Model contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute system commands via the deviceName POST parameter.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Tenda AC7, AC9, and AC10 Routers Command Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Tenda AC7, AC9, and AC10 devices contain a command injection vulnerability due to  the "formsetUsbUnload" function executes a dosystemCmd function with untrusted input. Successful exploitation allows an attacker to execute OS commands via a crafted goform/setUsbUnload request.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: ThinkPHP "noneCms" Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: ThinkPHP "noneCms" contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution through crafted use of the filter parameter.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: ThinkPHP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: ThinkPHP contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution via public//?s=index/\think\app/invokefunction&function=call_user_func_array&vars[0]=system&vars[1][]= followed by the command.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro OfficeScan Directory Traversal Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro OfficeScan contains a directory traversal vulnerability by extracting files from a zip file to a specific folder on the OfficeScan server, leading to remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro Apex One and OfficeScan Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro Apex One and OfficeScan contain an unspecified vulnerability within a migration tool component that allows for remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.product: Apex One, OfficeScan and Worry-Free Business Security Agents
cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro Multiple Products Content Validation Escape Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro Apex One, OfficeScan, and Worry-Free Business Security agents contain a content validation escape vulnerability that could allow an attacker to manipulate certain agent client components.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.product: Apex One, OfficeScan, and Worry-Free Business Security
cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro Multiple Products Improper Access Control Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro Apex One, OfficeScan, and Worry-Free Business Security on Microsoft Windows contain an improper access control vulnerability that may allow an attacker to manipulate a particular product folder to disable the security temporarily, abuse a specific Windows function, and attain privilege escalation.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro Apex One and OfficeScan Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro Apex One and OfficeScan server contain a vulnerable EXE file that could allow a remote attacker to write data to a path on affected installations and bypass root login.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.product: Apex One, Apex One as a Service, and Worry-Free Business Security
cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro Multiple Products Improper Input Validation Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro Apex One, Apex One as a Service, and Worry-Free Business Security contain an improper input validation vulnerability that allows for privilege escalation.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.product: Apex One, Apex One as a Service, and Worry-Free Business Security
cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Trend Micro Multiple Products Improper Input Validation Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Trend Micro Apex One, Apex One as a Service, and Worry-Free Business Security contain an improper input validation vulnerability that allows a remote attacker to upload files.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: TVT NVMS-1000 Directory Traversal Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: TVT devices utilizing NVMS-1000 software contain a directory traversal vulnerability via GET /.. requests.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Unraid Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Unraid contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to gain access to the administrative interface. This CVE is chainable with CVE-2020-5847 for remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Unraid Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Unraid contains a vulnerability due to the insecure use of the extract PHP function that can be abused to execute remote code as root. This CVE is chainable with CVE-2020-5849 for initial access.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: vBulletin PHP Module Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: The PHP module within vBulletin contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution via the widgetConfig[code] parameter in an ajax/render/widget_php routestring request.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: vBulletin PHP Module Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: The PHP module within vBulletin contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution via crafted subWidgets data in an ajax/render/widget_tabbedcontainer_tab_panel request. This CVE ID resolves an incomplete patch for CVE-2019-16759.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware ESXi and Horizon DaaS OpenSLP Heap-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware ESXi and Horizon Desktop as a Service (DaaS) OpenSLP contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows an attacker with network access to port 427 to overwrite the heap of the OpenSLP service to perform remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware ESXi OpenSLP Use-After-Free Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware ESXi OpenSLP contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows an attacker residing in the management network with access to port 427 to perform remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware Multiple Products Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware Fusion, Remote Console (VMRC) for Mac, and Horizon Client for Mac contain a privilege escalation vulnerability due to improper use of setuid binaries that allows attackers to escalate privileges to root.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware vCenter Server File Upload Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware vCenter Server contains a file upload vulnerability in the Analytics service that allows a user with network access to port 443 to execute code.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware vCenter Server Information Disclosure Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware vCenter Server contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service (vmdir) when the Platform Services Controller (PSC) does not correctly implement access controls. Successful exploitation allows an attacker with network access to port 389 to extract sensitive information.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware vCenter Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware vCenter Server vSphere Client contains a remote code execution vulnerability in a vCenter Server plugin which allows an attacker with network access to port 443 to execute commands with unrestricted privileges on the underlying operating system.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: VMware vCenter Server Improper Input Validation Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware vSphere Client contains an improper input validation vulnerability in the Virtual SAN Health Check plug-in, which is enabled by default in vCenter Server, which allows for remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Multiple VMware Products Command Injection Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: VMware Workspace One Access, Access Connector, Identity Manager, and Identity Manager Connector contain a command injection vulnerability. An attacker with network access to the administrative configurator on port 8443 and a valid password for the configurator administrator account can execute commands with unrestricted privileges on the underlying operating system.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: WordPress File Manager Plugin Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: WordPress File Manager plugin contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated users to execute PHP code and upload malicious files on a target site.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: WordPress Snap Creek Duplicator Plugin File Download Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: WordPress Snap Creek Duplicator plugin contains a file download vulnerability when an administrator creates a new copy of their site that allows an attacker to download the generated files from their Wordpress dashboard. This vulnerability affects Duplicator and Dulplicator Pro.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: WordPress Social Warfare Plugin Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: WordPress Social Warfare plugin contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability that allows for remote code execution. This vulnerability affects Social Warfare and Social Warfare Pro.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Yealink Device Management Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Yealink Device Management contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus contains an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting the REST API URLs which allow for remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central File Upload Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central contains a file upload vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Zoho ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus (SDP) File Upload Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Zoho ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus (SDP) contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows remote users to upload files via login page customization.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_catalog.vulnerabilityName: Zyxel Multiple Products Use of Hard-Coded Credentials Vulnerability
cisa_kev_catalog.shortDescription: Zyxel firewalls (ATP, USG, VM) and AP Controllers (NXC2500 and NXC5500) contain a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability in an undocumented account ("zyfwp") with an unchangeable password.
cisa_kev_catalog.requiredAction: Apply updates per vendor instructions.

cisa_kev_added_last_7_days.shortDescription: Optimizely Web Experimentation contains an external control of critical state data vulnerability in its account signup flow that could allow an attacker to impersonate existing customer users and modify Project JavaScript. items.title: Microsoft confirms authentication issues after November updates
items.summary: Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability. [...]
items.details:
Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability.

Tracked as CVE-2026-118737 , this security flaw was found in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime and stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to remotely execute code without user interaction on unpatched systems.

Microsoft says the November security updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, which reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing.

However, as Microsoft explained in an updated support document, the new security improvements introduced to address this vulnerability may also cause authentication failures on patched devices.

"Microsoft is aware of compatibility issues affecting some third-party apps and devices, including authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) solutions, and application packaging solutions that use NTLM authentication," it said.

"This issue can occur when such a proxy device does not correctly implement the NTLM protocol. For example, an affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field."

While a fix is not yet available, Microsoft said affected apps and devices return an NTLMSSP_CHALLENGE message with an empty "Target Info List" in network trace signatures or Target Machine fields with "Not Found" values in event logs.

As a temporary workaround, the company advised customers to go through the following procedure on affected systems:

Set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm REG_DWORD registry value under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 to 1 (the value used for clients that do not offer SIGN)

Check whether the affected device or application supports a configuration that uses Kerberos authentication or whether the vendor provides a software or firmware update compatible with the NTLM signing requirements introduced by CVE-2026-118737 .

If neither option is available, contact the device or software vendor to request an update that complies with the NTLM protocol requirements described in 3.1.5.1.2 Client Receives a CHALLENGE_MESSAGE from the Server .

However, Microsoft said the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm registry setting is a short-term solution and may be removed in the future.

"Updating the affected product or using a compatible authentication configuration is the recommended long-term resolution," it noted.

Since it addressed installation issues affecting the November 2026 cumulative updates, Microsoft has also confirmed that this month's security updates are causing Windows activation failures and SQL Server performance issues .

The company is also investigating a known issue that may break printing documents with complex formatting for customers who have installed the latest Windows updates.

items.title: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system
items.summary: Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) [...]
items.details:
Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)

​Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), according to a source familiar with the matter.

The source told The New York Times , which first reported the incident, that the cyberattack was carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.

While the CIA and the ODNI have not yet replied to a request for more details regarding this incident, no classified data or systems were exposed in the breach.

"The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk," the source said.

Hours after the CIA security breach was reported, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) also disclosed that it's investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. After detecting the attack, the agency took some systems offline as a precaution and told banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports, since some services may be unavailable.

FinCEN is a US Department of the Treasury bureau that acts as the country's official Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and protects the nation's financial system from illicit activities by sharing financial intelligence with law enforcement agencies both domestically and internationally.

BleepingComputer reached out to a FinCEN spokesperson with questions about the incident, but a response was not immediately available.

One week ago, the US National Security Agency's classified network also suffered a days-long outage , but the agency blamed scheduled routine maintenance and said its mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational.

These incidents follow a series of other cyberattacks that have led to security breaches at other US federal agencies in recent years.

For instance, two years ago, the Silk Typhoon Chinese state-backed hacking group hacked the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) , another Treasury Department office that administers economic and trade sanctions programs.

The same threat group also breached the Treasury's Office of Financial Research , and it reportedly infiltrated the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (a Treasury Department office that reviews foreign investments for national security risks).

More recently, as BleepingComputer reported over the weekend, hackers reportedly breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) . However, it is unclear how the attackers gained access, when the breach occurred, or whether they stole any information from the compromised systems.

This follows a claim by the ShinyHunters extortion group that it breached the FBI's recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, prompting an FBI investigation that led to the arrests of multiple suspected ShinyHunters members , including a Canadian cybersecurity executive reportedly linked to the attack.

items.title: Hackers Compromise 24 Check Point Management Servers in Suspected AI-Driven Attack Campaign
items.summary: An unknown threat actor has been using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven offensive tooling in a campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, impacting 22 distinct organizations across the world. The intrusion activity, tracked by GreyNoise under the moniker GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13), is assessed to have targeted organizations in the financial services, energy, government,
items.details:
GreyNoise links a campaign affecting 22 organizations and targeting Check Point Management servers to suspected AI-driven offensive tooling.

An unknown threat actor has been using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven offensive tooling in a campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, impacting 22 distinct organizations across the world.

The intrusion activity, tracked by GreyNoise under the moniker GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13), is assessed to have targeted organizations in the financial services, energy, government, transportation, mining, engineering, and manufacturing sectors across the U.K., Ireland, France, Netherlands, Greece, Germany, Austria, Bulgaria, Poland, India, Thailand, Vietnam, South Korea, Hong Kong, China, Australia, and the U.S.

Confirmed attack activity has been recorded between October 17 and November 2, 2026, with the threat actor using 99 IP addresses to conduct scanning, exploitation, and control. Most of these IP addresses are associated with disposable network infrastructure.

The campaign has not been attributed to any known threat actor or group. It's suspected that the attackers are relying on agentic harnesses and systems for vulnerability scanning, exploitation, and automatic interaction with compromised assets.

The threat actor has also been observed using tools like Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and other Python scripts to carry out internal reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement on victim environments.

"We witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created," GreyNoise said.

In one case, the attackers have been found using an automated scanning and exploitation pipeline to compromise an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500 , a critical flaw in Rejetto HFS, in early October 2026 to obtain control of the server and issue commands, including adding an SSH key to the "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" file.

Subsequently, GT13 is said to have used the compromised server as a relay for follow-on operations centered around saving command results and exfiltrating data from 24 previously compromised Check Point Security Management servers. The attackers also unsuccessfully attempted to deploy a Linux implant named ZULT to the compromised Rejetto HFS server.

"The GT13 adversary had access to the victim Check Point Security Management Servers before they compromised the HFS server," the cybersecurity company said. "We could not determine when or how the attacker gained access to those Check Point assets."

The attackers also moved to burrow deeper into one of the victim networks, using a script for a now-patched Check Point flaw ( CVE-2026-16232 ) to launch over 100 management tasks on multiple Check Point Management Servers to -

Steal firewall databases and internal certificate authority files

Unload security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections

Conduct internal network reconnaissance and attempt lateral movement

The post-compromise activity also involved attempts to target other enterprise systems, such as Citrix NetScaler ( CVE-2023-4966 ), Ivanti Connect Secure ( CVE-2024-21893 ), VMware vCenter ( CVE-2021-21972 and CVE-2023-34048 ), Microsoft Exchange ( CVE-2021-26855 and CVE-2021-34473 ), and Microsoft Netlogon ( CVE-2020-1472 ).

In tandem, the threat actor has attempted to exploit various other security flaws, including, but not limited to -

GreyNoise has theorized that GT13 has in its possession a "mature AI-enabled offensive apparatus" that it uses to weaponize vulnerabilities, scan for susceptible assets, and exploit them to gain access to systems that can be later used as operational relays or true targets.

"The activity reported by the GreyNoise article involves CVE-2026-16232, a previously disclosed vulnerability with patches already available, and does not represent a new vulnerability or exploitation technique," Sergey Shykevich, Director, Threat Intelligence at Check Point Software Technologies, told The Hacker News.

"Our priority remains ensuring customers apply the available updates and follow Check Point’s published hardening guidance to restrict management access and identify suspicious activity."

items.details:
Com-affiliated hackers use vishing, session hijacking, and unauthorized MFA enrollment to steal corporate cloud data and extort victims.

Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has disclosed that it's tracking and has responded to "numerous waves of vishing attacks" orchestrated by Com-affiliated threat actors since August 2026 that have led to data theft and extortion attempts.

The attacks have targeted financial services, healthcare, and legal services located in the U.S., the U.K., and Australia. Other targets include construction, high-technology, transportation, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, insurance, and real estate sectors.

"The victims share a common profile: they hold large volumes of high-impact corporate data where exposure carries severe regulatory, legal, or market consequences," Unit 42 said . "These attackers targeted financial services organizations about twice as often as healthcare organizations in August 2026, but healthcare overtook financial services in September."

The activity has been attributed to a number of threat clusters , including -

CL-CRI-1116 (aka Redact, formerly BlackFile), first observed in January 2026

CL-CRI-1192 (aka Helix and UNC6671), first observed in June 2026

CL-CRI-1264 (aka Vortex), first observed in September 2026

CL-CRI-1274 (aka Cinder), first observed in September 2026

Intrusions typically commence with voice phishing, with the attackers posing as IT staff to resolve a purported authentication issue and direct the victim to a phishing page personalized to their organization.

Once the AiTM kit captures credentials and session tokens, the attackers quickly enroll their own multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, abuse cloud utilities and, in a few instances, deploy malicious browser extensions to exfiltrate data and extort victims.

The harvested authentication data is used to authenticate to victim environments, typically by routing such requests through residential proxy networks and commercial VPNs. They then seek to establish multi-layered persistence by registering their MFA devices, generating cloud infrastructure temporary credentials, authorizing unapproved third-party OAuth applications; enumerate sensitive data; evade defenses by modifying mailbox rules and clearing security alert events; and harvest data from cloud platforms.

"Attackers associated with CL-CRI-1264 establish initial access through vishing, where they pose as internal IT support and direct employees to servers using subdomains tailored to each targeted organization," Unit 42 said.

"These servers act as adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) proxies that pass user credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) approvals to the attackers in real time. Attackers have targeted employees on both their corporate workstations and personal mobile devices."

CL-CRI-1264 has also been observed enrolling unauthorized MFA devices within minutes of authenticating to establish persistence, often reusing a single device named Pixel 10a across compromised accounts. The attack chains involve automated data exfiltration using Python scripts to harvest information from Microsoft 365 mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint.

Once data is exfiltrated, the threat actor sends Microsoft Teams messages directly to employees at victim organizations, claiming data theft and instructing them to visit a TOR-hosted ransom negotiation site.

The second new cluster to emerge around the same time is CL-CRI-1274, which has also leaned on vishing for initial access and leveraged the Microsoft Graph software development kit (SDK) to collect and exfiltrate data from the victim's SharePoint and OneDrive environments.

"Afterwards, the attackers used a compromised account to send extortion messages internally via email and Microsoft Teams, ultimately directing recipients to a Tor-hosted negotiation site," Unit 42 said.

items.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
items.summary: WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account. The WordPress plugins team has independently detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released. Visiting each plugin listing now
items.details:
WordPress blocked malicious releases of six WP Connect plugins containing backdoors designed to enable arbitrary code execution.

WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account.

The WordPress plugins team has independently detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released. Visiting each plugin listing now serves the message: "This plugin has been closed as of November 22, 2026, and is not available for download. This closure is permanent."

The names of the affected plugins and the malicious versions are listed below -

These plugins have been collectively installed on more than 3,600 WordPress sites, according to WordPress security company Wordfence. The supply chain compromise is being tracked as CVE-2026-135202 (CVSS score: 9.8). It remains unpatched.

"Each release silently loaded the same remote-control module, which phones home to an attacker-controlled server, executes any PHP code it is sent, and exposes a full command set for running shell commands, stealing password hashes, and planting webshells," security researcher Chloe Chamberland said .

Specifically, the plugins come with a backdoor module ("includes/airwp-online.php") that runs on every request, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress, and OS versions, and the server user) to a hard-coded command-and-control server ("tascredit-pay[.]com"), and runs PHP code returned by the server via eval().

Dump the users table including login, email address, and password hashes

Drop a web shell into the uploads directory or to a path of the attacker's choosing

Register an hourly WP-Cron hook that runs attacker-supplied code

As a result, an unauthenticated attacker in control of the site can execute arbitrary code on the server and take complete control, facilitating credential theft and persistence through web shells and cron hooks that outlast the plugin removal.

Because the malicious versions were never released and blocked due to WordPress's new cooldown protections as part of its Protect The Shire initiative, sites running these plugins are unlikely to be affected. However, it's essential that site owners check their websites to make sure that they are not running one of the compromised versions and remove them as soon as possible.

"Unlike a typical vulnerability, this was not a coding mistake, and there is no patch: the malicious code was added deliberately and committed to each plugin's WordPress.org repository," Chamberland. "Taken together, this strongly suggests that the developer's WordPress.org account was compromised and used to push the malicious releases, rather than that the vendor shipped this code intentionally."

The disclosure comes as URLscan.io revealed that an unspecified WordPress site had been infected by multiple cybercriminal campaigns, with attackers attempting to disable or remove scripts belonging to competing threat actors.

The site carried "thirteen separate ClickFix injections from three distinct kits [LOM, ErrTraffic, and Macfinger], alongside seven further malicious loaders," it said . "Several of the injections attempt to remove each other's code and overlays, and one injection disables another through a JavaScript naming collision. Five of the thirteen injections resolve their next-stage infrastructure from Polygon smart contracts, a technique known as EtherHiding ."
